 🚀 Thanks to a Serbian midriff! Klopp's side make a flying start 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Germany are under pressure in the Nations League. Given the group standings, they need two wins against Serbia and the Netherlands. Even then, qualification is not guaranteed.
 Today's match against Serbia kicked off at 20:45, and Germany got off to an explosive start. Their opponents certainly gave them a helping hand, though. 
 OneFootball Videos
 Serbia 0 Germany 2 45+2' Following a corner, their first foray into the opposition penalty area, Kai Havertz met Mittelstädt's cross with a completely unmarked header. The ball then deflected off Babić's lower abdomen before ending up in the net. Ultimately, it was an unfortunate own goal that put Germany in a comfortable position as early as the third minute.
 📸 PEDJA MILOSAVLJEVIC - AFP or licensors
 VAR did intervene to check a possible handball by Thiaw, but the goal stood.
 Can Germany extend their lead in the Belgrade rain? Let us know in the comments!
